subject: how to restart gl.report.ld.map after it maxes out memory

messages.author: b40d9a0724dacefc
messages.subject: how to restart gl.report.ld.map after it maxes out memory
parts:
Hello,
I ran gl.report.ld.map() and it completed for 16 of my 18 populations and then maxed out for memory use.  Is there a way to restart and just have the command finish the last 2.  I do have access to the full output so far in the tempdir().

Thank you.

messages.author: 592079bda2cb3220
messages.subject: Re: how to restart gl.report.ld.map after it maxes out memory
parts:
Hi,

You can try:

library(dartR.base)
t1 <- platypus.gl
#population names
popNames(t1)
#subsetting populations
t1_pop_1_2 <- gl.keep.pop(t1,pop.list = c("SEVERN_ABOVE" ,"SEVERN_BELOW"))
#running LD report
res <- gl.report.ld.map(t1_pop_1_2)
# Saving R object
saveRDS(res,"results_ld.rds")
# reading R object
res_ld <- readRDS("results_ld.rds")


Also, note that when you close your RStudio session, the tempdir is deleted. 
If you run out of the memory you can remove all the objects of your environment and reset your RStudio session.
1 Save the R objects you want to keep as shown above. 
2 Menu > Session > Clear Workspace > Yes
3 Menu > Session > Restart R

Cheers,
Luis

messages.author: 592079bda2cb3220
messages.subject: Re: how to restart gl.report.ld.map after it maxes out memory
parts:
Yes, something like this:

library(dartRverse)
t1 <- gl.filter.callrate(platypus.gl,threshold = 1)
t1 <- gl.filter.monomorphs(t1)
t1 <- gl.filter.maf(t1,threshold = 0.1)
popNames(t1)
pop1 <- gl.keep.pop(t1,pop.list = "SEVERN_ABOVE")
pop2 <- gl.keep.pop(t1,pop.list = "SEVERN_BELOW")
pop3 <- gl.keep.pop(t1,pop.list = "TENTERFIELD")
ld_1 <- gl.report.ld.map(pop1)
ld_2 <- gl.report.ld.map(pop2)
ld_3 <- gl.report.ld.map(pop3)
ld_tmp <- rbind(ld_1,ld_2)
ld_fin <- rbind(ld_tmp,ld_3)

t2 <- gl.filter.ld(t1,ld.report = ld_fin)
